proposedWebsiteFields.name: Tre Cime di Lavaredo classic circuit
proposedWebsiteFields.desc:
A demanding 9.528 km circuit from Rifugio Auronzo around the Tre Cime, following trails 101 and 105. The official itinerary gives 468 m of ascent, about 3 hours 30 minutes and a high point of 2,454 m. This is a hard, open high-alpine walk rather than a casual sightseeing loop.

Dogs are accepted on the route but must stay on lead throughout. Seasonal livestock may be present beside the Lavaredo pasture segment, so keep your dog close and pass animals conservatively. The route has very little dependable shade and includes a narrower section, although no ferrata equipment is required.
proposedWebsiteFields.tips: Start and finish at Rifugio Auronzo. The seasonal toll road and parking are weather-dependent and normally require advance booking; roadside parking is prohibited. Carry sufficient water. A fountain is identified at Malga LangAlm, but its seasonal availability and potability are not guaranteed.
proposedWebsiteFields.imageCredit: Tre Cime di Lavaredo, Sentiero per il Rifugio Locatelli — Simone A. Bertinotti — CC BY-SA 4.0 — via Wikimedia Commons
proposedWebsiteFields.imageAlt: Gravel trail towards Rifugio Locatelli beneath the Tre Cime di Lavaredo peaks.
proposedWebsiteFields.terrainType: High-alpine dirt and rocky mountain paths, including one narrower section

proposedWebsiteFields.name: Cinque Torri three-refuges assisted circuit
proposedWebsiteFields.desc:
This chairlift-assisted circuit begins at Bai de Dones, rises on the 5 Torri lift and returns on foot through the Cinque Torri open-air museum, refuge area and forest. The approved track contains 1.37 km of lift transport followed by approximately 3.95 km of predominantly downhill walking, with about two hours allowed for the itinerary.

Dogs of any size may use the 5 Torri lift free of charge, but both leash and muzzle are required. The upper museum and refuge area is open alpine terrain, while the lower return enters forest. Seasonal sheep grazing is documented in the wider area, so keep dogs close even though an encounter on the exact circuit is variable.
proposedWebsiteFields.tips: This itinerary depends on the 5 Torri chairlift operating. The published 2026 season is 6 June to 11 October, subject to weather and snow. Use the approved Bai de Dones parking pin. Carry water: the three refuges are possible service stops, but no freely accessible potable dog-water point has been verified.
proposedWebsiteFields.imageCredit: Cinque Torri 01 — Clemens Stockner — CC BY-SA 4.0 — via Wikimedia Commons
proposedWebsiteFields.imageAlt: The Cinque Torri rock towers viewed from the west in the Ampezzo Dolomites.
proposedWebsiteFields.terrainType: Museum and trench paths, cart track and forest hiking path
